title: Connection Pools and Resource Management
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of connection pools and resource management in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply connection pools and resource management in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to timeouts and failure handling and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Connection Pools and Resource Management through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding connection pools and resource management helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Connection Pools and Resource Management helps you reason about reusing database connections. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Reusing database connections. Then connect it to Pool sizing concepts. The remaining syllabus points—Connection cleanup, Timeouts and failure handling—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Connection Pools and Resource Management
content_blocks.code:
require "sqlite3"
db = SQLite3::Database.new(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE TABLE tasks (id INTEGER, title TEXT)")
db.execute("INSERT INTO tasks VALUES (?, ?)", [1, "Learn Ruby"])
puts db.get_first_value("SELECT title FROM tasks WHERE id = ?", 1)
db.close
